errorCodes.meaning: The caller is not permitted to forget memory in the named context.
The `expectedVersion` precondition failed. The details carry the maintainer's current version and value, so the caller can see the edit it was about to discard.

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

MemoryKey.description: Agent-chosen identifier for an item within a context. Opaque to the maintainer: it MUST NOT be parsed, normalized, or case-folded, and prefix matching in `vta/memory/list` is a byte-prefix comparison over the UTF-8 encoding. Agents SHOULD use `/`-delimited hierarchical keys (`contact/billing`, `preference/timezone`) so that `prefix` can address a family of items, but the delimiter is a convention between an agent and itself. A key is content as well as an address: a key naming a person, a condition or a dispute discloses something to anyone who can list the context, even without its value.
MemoryKey.title: MemoryKey

MemoryVersion.description: A value of the context's monotonic write counter (see this schema's description). Server-assigned; a producer never chooses one.
MemoryVersion.title: MemoryVersion

deletedAt.description: When the deletion was recorded. Absent on the same terms as `version`.

existed.description: True when a live item was removed by this request. False when the key already held a tombstone, or held nothing at all — both of which are successes, because the caller's intent is satisfied either way.

version.description: The tombstone's version — the counter value this delete took, or the value the existing tombstone already held when `existed` is false. Absent only when the key held nothing and no tombstone was written.

schema.description: Forget one memory item. The item's value is discarded and a tombstone takes its place for the maintainer's retention window, so that another device syncing the context learns of the deletion instead of keeping a copy forever.

contextId.description: The VTA context the item lives in.

expectedVersion.description: Optional precondition, on the same terms as vta/memory/put: the live item must be at exactly this version, so a delete cannot discard an edit the caller never saw. Positive only — a create-only precondition on a delete can never be useful, so the schema does not admit 0.
